page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.medium is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) running at 2.8 GHz, with 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. It includes 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core capabilities and multi-threaded or memory-intensive workloads. Single-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1694.58 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1741.0. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.0 GB/sec. However, because the instance is limited to a single vCPU, multi-core benchmarks are poor, as seen in the Geekbench multi-core score of 1736.0. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached large-block write speeds at 11.68 GB/sec and read speeds at 30.06 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8gd.medium offers a low-entry point to the Graviton8 memory-optimized family, bundling dedicated ARMv9 compute with local NVMe SSD storage. This resource density makes it suitable for lightweight, memory-sensitive workloads that require fast local scratch space but do not demand high parallel processing power. Appropriate workloads include small-scale database operations, caching layers, lightweight text processing, and single-threaded utility scripts.
